item.ptxt: Using TaSCAN, check mode as well as normal mode can be selected, which increases malfunction detection sensitivity compared to normal mode.
Perform inspection in check mode when a malfunction is suspected in a sensor signal circuit but the normal code is output in normal mode.

atten4.ptxt: If the SST (TaSCAN) display is abnormal, refer to .

step2.ptxt: Following the SST (TaSCAN) screen display, select Main Menu [Diagnosis] → Diagnosis Menu [Powertrain] → [TCCS] → System Diagnosis Menu [Mode Change], and select normal mode or check mode.
Following the SST (TaSCAN) screen display, select Main Menu [Diagnosis] → Diagnosis Menu [Powertrain] → [TCCS] → System Diagnosis Menu [DTC Freeze Frame Data], and check the DTCs.

item.ptxt: DTCs indicating provisional malfunctions
Although a malfunction has not been confirmed, the possibility of a malfunction can be known.

atten4.ptxt: A provisional malfunction means that, for DTCs detected with 2-trip detection logic (such as P0171/25), the engine control computer stores a malfunction on the 1 trip as a provisional malfunction.

step1.ptxt: DTC Check (Reading Using Check Engine Warning Light)

item.ptxt: Before reading DTCs, turn the IG ON and check that the check engine warning light comes on.
Inspection in check mode cannot be performed.

step2.ptxt: Using SST (diagnosis check wire No.2), connect between terminals 13 (TC) ←→ 4 (CG) of the DLC3.

atten3.ptxt: • Connecting the connector to the wrong position will cause a malfunction, so never make a mistake.
• Use only the dedicated SST (diagnosis check wire No. 2).

step2.ptxt: Turn the IG ON and read the number of blinks of the check engine warning light.

atten3.ptxt: When letters are used in a TCCS code, such as [A7], the code is expressed as a 2-digit base-16 number; in this case, the light blinks 10 times and then blinks 7 times. (Blinking intervals are the same)

item.ptxt: If no code is displayed (the light does not blink), a malfunction in the TC terminal circuit, a malfunction in the VC terminal circuit or a computer malfunction is suspected.
If the check engine warning light remains on, a short in the wire harness (pinched, etc.) or a computer malfunction is suspected.
If a meaningless code is output, a computer malfunction is suspected.
If the check engine warning light comes on at 1000r/min or more and no code is output, turn the IG OFF once and then inspect again.

step2.ptxt: Remove the SST (diagnosis check wire No. 2).
Using TaSCAN, operate according to the screen display and select a DTC recording freeze data (F displayed) from the [Diagnosis] → [DTC Check] screen.

item.ptxt: Time-series freeze data allows the engine condition (ECU data) before and after DTC detection to be checked.
Using time-series freeze data is useful for troubleshooting when the symptom cannot be reproduced.

step2.ptxt: Operate according to the screen display to display the [Diagnosis] → [DTC Freeze Data] screen, and clear the DTCs.

item.ptxt: If they cannot be cleared, turn the IG OFF once and then try again.
Do not clear DTCs using TaSCAN until the cause has been identified.
When clearing, save the detected data.

step2.ptxt: Remove the EFI MAIN fuse (20A) and ETCS fuse (10A), and reinstall the fuses after 60 seconds or more have elapsed.

item.ptxt: After inspecting and repairing the EFI system, always clear the DTC memory and then check that the normal code is output.
Do not clear DTCs by removing fuses until the cause has been identified.

step1.ptxt: Check Diagnosis Judgment Results (Checking Using TaSCAN)

item.ptxt: Whether DTC judgment has been completed can be checked using SST (TaSCAN).
This can be used for reproduction tests of malfunctions by DTC output and for confirmation after repairs are completed.

step2.ptxt: Perform a road test to execute the diagnosis judgment check.
Following the SST (TaSCAN) screen instructions, select Main Menu [Diagnosis] → Diagnosis Menu [Powertrain] → [TCCS] → System Diagnosis Menu [Diagnosis Judgment Result Check] → [Check by DTC].
On the next screen, enter the DTC to be checked.
